title: Finding simple flavour beyond ideal leisure

captions.physics: Changing a view of familiar enjoyment
captions.energy: Following a vague ideal of experience
captions.emotions: Feeling fullness in available shared pleasure

meaning: Changed leisure can feel rich when a vague ideal yields to a simple enjoyment both already share freely.
text: Sometimes another perspective reveals pleasure already nearby. The Hanged Man in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps pause a habitual search and examine another way of resting. The Moon in energy leans towards a vague picture of the desired impression. The Empress in emotions allows fullness in what is available. That fullness needs no special-looking evening. Fresh attention to a familiar flavour or small detail can be enough, beyond overlooking it for a more promising programme and an unclear ideal of what enjoyment ought to be.

For example, instead of seeking an unusual dessert, you try ordinary apples cut into different shapes and compare impressions. The idea initially seems too modest. **A simple shared flavour can bring a real sense of fullness.** You notice crispness, scent and amusing differences in the pieces. Another perspective makes the familiar alive, while conversation gives pleasure a shared form without immediately adding a recipe, special dishes or an entire table of treats.

The difficulty is continuing comparison with a picture nobody can describe clearly. Pleasure already exists while you seek a missing detail, letting conjecture obscure what was received. A changed perspective helps recognise sufficiency. Value need not match outward scale. A small idea can be complete leisure when both freely taste and name what delighted them without first proving sufficient novelty or beauty.
